AAC-AD-No-2021-01-Boeing-737-8-and-737-9: A textbook reflow cascade. Everything is present and correctly drawn; the page simply starts a paragraph earlier than the reference — the sentence XRay.Office opens page 3 with is the one LibreOffice ends page 2 with — and the running header lands mid-page as a result. The page count is identical, so the drift resolves itself later in the document.
150_5300_13_chg10.doc: Two-column body text set slightly tighter than the reference, so each column carries more lines and the page ends at a different paragraph. The revision change-bars are drawn in both. XRay.Office also prints a chapter marker in the footer that the reference leaves blank — the extra ink the metric picked up.
UG.CAO.00006 Foreign Part 145 approvals: Two distinct defects on one page. The viewer draws the document's header table — agency logo, document number, approval date — on a page where the reference suppresses it; and the footer's page-number field resolves to Page 29 of 29 where the reference prints Page 4 of 29. A page-number field that returns the last page rather than the current one is the classic symptom of a field parsed but never evaluated.
approvals-and-standardisation-organisati: The automatic numbering in the ID column runs 1–13 in the reference and 1–9, then 12–16 in the viewer: the list counter is advancing on rows that carry no number of their own. Row heights are also taller throughout, which is why the document runs to seven pages against the reference's six — and why the footer's total disagrees.
087_Printable_Graph_Paper_Template_Green: A page that is almost entirely fine rule. Both engines draw the grid; the viewer's rows are compressed against the reference's, so every line lands a fraction off and the structural metric collapses. This is the class of page where a low SSIM says least — and why nothing here is ranked on SSIM alone.
Demick_JetBlue.pptx: Every bullet glyph is a missing-glyph box: the symbol font the bullets are specified in is not resolved, so the renderer draws the fallback tofu. The body face is also a sans where the reference uses a serif, which is why the same text takes fewer lines. The subtle paper texture behind the reference is absent.
redac-fullComm-201705-EE-FRs-briefing.pp: The same missing bullet-glyph defect as the JetBlue deck, on an unrelated presentation and a different template — a systematic gap in bullet-font resolution rather than one bad file. Line breaks differ for the same reason: a substituted body face.
N2_E_Maestroni_Swarm_COP.pptx: The reference and XRay.Office both apply the picture's washout recolour, laying the title over a faded satellite image. The viewer draws the same image at full saturation, so the dark-blue title all but disappears into it, and the title does not wrap where the other two break it. Worth noting that on this one the viewer may be closer to PowerPoint — but LibreOffice is the reference here.
Sector_Skills_Insights_Advanced_Manufact: Nothing is missing, mis-coloured or mis-ordered. The text block is inset slightly further from the left and the glyphs run a shade wider, so every line breaks a word or two earlier than the reference. This is what the worst end of the XRay.Office slide distribution actually looks like.
429_BLISc 2019 IInd Sem. PAPER-7 UNIT 3: The body placeholder is laid out wider than the reference's, running under the template's green graphic, so justified lines break later and the whole block finishes higher up the slide. Content, bullets and colour all match.
airports_6.xlsx: Row heights diverge where a cell's text wraps: the reference gives “California Redwood Coast-Humboldt County” two lines and XRay.Office one, so more rows fit and the page carries different records. The footer is the sharper defect — the reference prints Page 2, XRay.Office prints Page with the number missing.
047_Date_tracker_Gantt_chart_bf34f3a8.xl: The chart's plot area is filled black where the reference leaves it white, and every data label reads [CELLRANGE] — the label's cell reference is being printed instead of resolved. The reference paginates this workbook to eight pages and XRay.Office to five, so the page numbering diverges too.
CSJU List of Recipients of funds 2013-20: One extra page early in a 96-page workbook shifts every page after it, so page 5 of each carries a different block of rows. The rendering itself is faithful; the pagination is off by one.
FY2021-AIP-grants.xlsx: Not a fidelity failure — a category difference. LibreOffice fits this wide sheet to paper, scaled down and broken across 58 landscape pages. The viewer has no print pagination: it draws the live grid at screen scale with row and column headers, gridlines and the sheet's autofilter controls. No alignment makes these two comparable as pages.
FY2023-AIP-grants.xlsx: The same structural difference as the other grant workbook: a paginated print rendering against a screen grid. The metric is measuring the difference between two kinds of artefact, not a rendering error.
